metadata.section: Chapter 23: Response When Inbreeding Pure-line Crosses
metadata.source_title: Evolution and Selection of Quantitative Traits

blocks.content: Considerable simplification occurs when two pure lines are crossed. In the resulting $ F_1 $, each locus will have only two segregating alleles (one from each line; both at frequency 1/2), and as a result, $ ^* = _D^2 $ and $ _DI^2 = _ ADI = 0 $ (Chapter 11). However, Equation 23.29 carries the unstated assumption that the environmental variance, $ _e^2 $, is unchanged over levels of inbreeding, which may not be correct (Chapter 17). More generally, $ _e^2 $ can be replaced by $ _e^2(t) $ to accommodate this concern. Note that any initial contribution to the selection response from dominance will quickly decay (as $ 2^ -n $).

For example, by generation 3 (n = 3), the remaining amount of response from selection in generations 0 and 1 are 6.662 and 9.318, respectively, for a total response of 15.98.
